subject: On-prem / Air-gapped qualification - hardware & offline ops follow-up

Subject: On-prem / Air-gapped qualification - hardware & offline ops follow-up

Hi Alice,

Thanks again for taking time today — really helpful conversation. Per our call, I wanted to capture the key notes and next steps so your IT/security and procurement teams have a clear summary.

Recap (from today):
- Goal: Deploy Redwood Private in an air-gapped on-prem environment for model inference (PII-sensitive loan processing).
- Preferred deployment: Private on-prem with airgap + customer-managed KMS. Hosted/Dedicated were discussed but ruled out because of data residency and network isolation requirements.
- Traffic profile: ~300 concurrent inference requests at peak, median request length ~128 tokens, bursty during batch overnight jobs.
- SLO targets: 95th latency < 350ms for typical requests; tolerable batch windows for longer jobs.

Open technical questions we agreed I'd follow up on:
1) Hardware compatibility and upgrade path — you're running a mixture of 3rd gen GPUs and want guidance for next 12–18 months.
2) Offline ops and maintenance process for air-gapped nodes (patching, model upgrades, KV/cache warming).
3) Initial network diagram + exact ports/protocols required for on-prem control-plane connectivity (if any) and allowed egress.

Attachments I’m sharing: network_diagram_v2.pdf (proposed architecture), redwood_onprem_architecture.pptx (detailed component doc), airgap_checklist.xlsx (prep checklist for your ops team).

Next steps:
- I’ll loop in Dev (cc’d) for hardware sizing + recommended upgrade list by EOD tomorrow.
- Please share a KMZ or network diagram with your firewall team or confirm any restrictions; Dev will produce a hardened list of required ports.
- If procurement wants an initial quote, I can pull together a Dedicated vs Private TCO comparison once we have the target rack/hardware.

Would you like us to schedule a follow-up tech deep-dive this week (30–45 mins)?

Thanks,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — this is great, and thanks for the clear summary. A couple quick clarifications before we loop in our infra leads: 

1) Hardware: our current fleet is mixed — a few NVIDIA A40s (older generation), 6 x A100s in two racks, and we're testing a small cluster with H100s in staging. We need guidance on whether we should standardize on A100s/H100s or if a mixed fleet is supported. We also have constraints on power per rack (18kW).

2) Offline ops: our security team requires a playbook for model upgrades that does not require internet connectivity. How do you handle model artifact transfer, KV cache priming, and rolling upgrades in an air-gapped environment?

3) Certificate/KMS: we use an on-prem HSM and Avro-based key wrapping. Can Redwood integrate with customer HSMs for KMS, or is there a proxy pattern required?

We’re OK to do a 30‑minute deep-dive with your SEs tomorrow morning (Tue 7/17 10:00 PT) — if that works for you and Dev.

Regards,
Alice Morgan
Director, AI Platforms | Legacy Bank
alice.morgan@legacybank.com | +1 (212) 555-0222

Date: Mon, 16 Jul 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On-prem / Air-gapped qualification - hardware & offline ops follow-up

Appreciate the details, Alice — good context. Quick answers inline below, and I’ll let Dev add specifics on the hardware tuning: 

1) Mixed fleet support: Redwood’s runtime supports mixed GPU fleets; however, for latency-sensitive inference we recommend standardizing on a compatible family (A100 or H100) where possible. We can provide a staged plan: keep current A40/A100s for non-critical/ETL inference and provision new H100s for low-latency production. Power-per-rack limits (18kW) are common — we’ll surface recommended node counts that respect that.

2) Offline ops and model upgrades: our Private deployment supports offline artifact transfer via signed bundle (tarball) and an airgap-side installer. The process we recommend:
- Create a signed model bundle (checked by your Ops/HSM).
- Transfer via secure media to the air-gapped environment.
- Use our offline installer to push new model artifacts to inference nodes; the controller coordinates rolling restarts and cache priming.
We’ll document the step-by-step playbook for your security team.

3) KMS/HSM integration: Yes — we support customer HSMs and KMS integrations. We have a connector pattern that uses a customer-managed KMS endpoint (mTLS) or an HSM proxy for wrapped keys. Dev will outline the exact auth flows supported.

Dev — can you provide a preliminary hardware upgrade recommendation (node counts, GPU types, NVMe sizing for KV cache) and an ops-runbook draft by EOD tomorrow? Alice — 10:00 PT Tuesday works for our team. I’ll send a calendar invite after Dev confirms.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: On-prem / Air-gapped qualification - hardware & offline ops follow-up

Hi Alice / Marissa,

Short version (preliminary):
- Recommendation: Standardize production inference racks on A100 80GB or H100 80GB depending on budget and single-token latency targets. Mixed fleet supported but expect ~10–18% latency variance between A100/H100 if the scheduler routes across families.
- Node counts: For your peak of ~300 concurrent requests (128-token median) we recommend 6 inference nodes (A100 80GB) with the following baseline: 8x vCPU, 512GB RAM, 25TB NVMe per node for KV/cache, 100GbE network fabric. If you choose H100, 4–5 nodes should suffice.
- Upgrades: For air-gapped upgrades we use: signed model bundles, checksum verification, staged canary on a single node, and rolling upgrade across racks. KV cache priming: we provide an offline cache snapshot that can be loaded prior to cutover.
- Power: A100 80GB dense config fits within 18kW per rack if you limit to 4–6 GPUs per chassis; we’ll provide a rack-level power spreadsheet.

I’ll attach the hardware spreadsheet and a skeleton ops-runbook in the doc I’ll upload to the Drive link. Plan for a 30–45 min technical deep-dive today 10:00 PT — I’ll share a calendar invite once Marissa confirms.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
